stem: A healthcare study measures average patient recovery rate across 4 hospitals, each containing multiple departments. hospital A has 8 observations with mean 63.8 % (within-hospital SD = 9.2). hospital B has 5 observations with mean 54.0 % (within-hospital SD = 3.5). hospital C has 10 observations with mean 48.8 % (within-hospital SD = 6.4). hospital D has 20 observations with mean 61.1 % (within-hospital SD = 3.5). The between-hospital standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 4.1 and 10.4 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average patient recovery rate for hospital A, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-hospital variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for hospital A: 62.7 % (shrunk from raw 63.8). Range [61.5, 63.3] as between-hospital SD varies from 4.1 to 10.4. Pooled mean: 57.9.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 57.9 % (weighted average of 4 hospital means).
Shrinkage factor for hospital A: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=6.9: B = 0.818.
Interval [61.5, 63.3] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (63.8) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (57.9) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
